programme.title: North East Dessert
programme.desc: It's the North East chefs' last chance to impress with the dessert course. It's been a week of highs and lows, modern audacious dishes and classic masterpieces but with only two places up for grabs cooking for the judges, at the end of today who will leave the competition empty-handed?

programme.title: North East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining North East chefs must cook all four courses again for the judges - Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They're joined by a guest judge - WI president Kirsty Bowen from Sheffield - who will help decide which chef will go through to represent the North East in the National Finals.

programme.title: North West Starter
programme.desc: Representing the North West are Eve Townson, Matt Worswick and returning contender Mark Ellis. Today's the starter course, and after failing to cook for the judges last year Mark's out to redeem himself, but he faces stiff competition in executive chef Eve and young gun Matt.

programme.title: North West Fish
programme.desc: It's the fish course, as three of the North West's finest chefs - Eve Townson, Matt Worswick and Mark Ellis - go head-to-head. Eve and Matt are hoping their classic approach to cooking fish will win the day whilst Mark is going all out with a fishy take on a traditional dessert recipe.

programme.title: North West Main
programme.desc: It's the battle for the main course for the three North West chefs - Eve Townson, Matt Worswick and Mark Ellis. Mark remains determined and focused on his battle to get to judges chamber this year, but as the pressure to plate up perfection reaches fever pitch, will all three chefs get a dish to the pass?

programme.title: North West Dessert
programme.desc: It's the North West chefs' last chance to impress, with the dessert course. Only two can cook for the judges tomorrow. It's the end of the road for one chef, but who will it be?

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining North West chefs cook their entire menus again for the judges Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They're joined by award-winning food writer Sabrina Ghayour, and together they'll decide which chef will go on to represent the North West in the National Finals.

programme.title: London South East Starter
programme.desc: It's the starter course for three of London and the South East's hottest chefs - Matt Gillan, Lee Westcott and Marcus Wareing's protégé Mark Froydenlund. Returning contender Matt Gillan is determined to make it to this year's banquet, but he faces fierce competition in the two newcomers.

programme.title: London South East Fish
programme.desc: The London and South East chefs - Matt Gillan, Lee Westcott and Marcus Wareing's protégé Mark Froydenlund - go head-to-head with their fish courses. Lee is hoping his modern plate of mackerel and passion fruit will outclass Matt and Mark's more traditionally inspired salmon dishes.

programme.title: London South East Main
programme.desc: It's a battle for the main course for three of London and the South East's finest chefs - Matt Gillan, Lee Westcott and Mark Froydenlund. Returning contender Matt is determined to bring home a 10 with his ambitious celebration of the billy goat but has he bitten off more than he can chew?

programme.title: London South East Dessert
programme.desc: It's dessert day and the London and South East chefs are striving to secure one of the two spots in tomorrow's Regional Final. The scores are close, so it's all to play for, as today marks the end of the competition for one man.

programme.title: London South East Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining London and South East chefs are cooking all four courses again for the judges - Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They're joined by Mary Gwynn, author of the official WI centenary cookbook. Together they'll decide which chef goes through to represent the region in the National Finals.

programme.title: Central Starter
programme.desc: Three of the Central Region's finest chefs - Pip Lacey, Richard Bainbridge and Jason Hodnett - attempt to impress this week's veteran judge with their starters. With big boots to fill, Angela Hartnett's protégé Pip is the only newcomer in the kitchen. Will she beat the boys to claim victory?

programme.title: Central Fish
programme.desc: The three Central Region chefs - newcomer Pip Lacey, 4th time competitor Richard Bainbridge and returning chef Jason Hodnett - fight it out in the fish course. Pip is hoping to outclass her rivals with a smoked haddock dish inspired by her Grandma.

programme.title: Central Main
programme.desc: It's a battle for the main course with three Central Region chefs - Pip Lacey, Richard Bainbridge and Jason Hodnett. Once again Jason is taking risks with his unusual collection of ingredients.

programme.title: Central Dessert
programme.desc: It's the last chance for the Central Region chefs to impress, with the dessert course. Only two chefs can go through to cook for the judges so with everything to play for, who will plate up perfection and who will be sent packing?

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining Central Region chefs cook their entire menus again for the judges - Prue Leith, Oliver Peyton and Matthew Fort. They'll be joined by former chair of the Women's Institute Helen Carey, who will help decide who will have the glory of representing the region in the National Finals.

programme.title: Finals Week: Starter
programme.desc: It's the starter course, and eight of the finest chefs in the country are battling it out to plate up impeccable dishes worthy of the Women's Institute. The judges are joined by WI Calendar Girl Angela Baker, but after Oliver reveals that this year it will be much tougher to make it onto the judge's shortlist, who will keep their cool and secure a place?

programme.title: Finals Week: Fish
programme.desc: It's the battle for the fish course. Those who failed to make it to the shortlist with their starters are hoping to do better. The judges are joined by Kristy Bowen, who knows the impeccable standards the WI will expect.

programme.title: Finals Week: Main
programme.desc: It's main course day, the half-way point in Finals Week, and those chefs who have yet to get a dish on the shortlist are feeling the heat. With only dishes judged to be perfect in with a chance at reaching the WI banquet, the standards are higher than ever before.

programme.title: Finals Week: Dessert
programme.desc: It's the last chance for the eight regional champions to get a dish in contention for the final banquet. Those who failed to make it to the shortlist are going all out. The judges are joined by Mary Gwynn, the author of the WI centenary cookbook.

programme.title: Finals Week: Banquet
programme.desc: The banquet is finally here. It's the culmination of months of hard work as the winning chefs strive to plate up perfect dishes for the Women's Institute ladies at London's historic Draper's Hall.

programme.title: Scotland Starter
programme.desc: Three top chefs from Scotland are out to impress this week's veteran judge and be crowned Scottish champion. Adam Handling has already won a number of industry awards and is full of confidence. His starter sets out to take the diner on a tour of the UK's best producers. He's up against Michael Bremner, who is hoping to impress with contemporary ingredients including Birch sap and Douglas fir oil. Ally McGrath is celebrating his nation's finest produce and making his very own version of haggis.

programme.title: Scotland Fish
programme.desc: Three newcomers to the competition create their fish dishes in a bid to be crowned Scottish champion. The standard is so high the veteran judge is moved to tears.

programme.title: Scotland Main
programme.desc: Ally McGrath has been keeping the veteran judge entertained with his very individual approach. Also, the highly competitive Adam Handling has been showcasing the finest produce grown and caught in and around the UK in his menu. Once again Michael Bremner is out to show how inventive he can be.

programme.title: Scotland Dessert
programme.desc: One chef will go home, and today the veteran judge finds himself with a difficult decision to make. Inventive chef Michael Bremner is recreating the Scottish desserts of his childhood, Adam Handling is sticking with his trademark Asian flavours and Ally McGrath is tempering chocolate for the very first time.

programme.title: Scotland Judging
programme.desc: Scotland's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for the judges for the very first time. Both chefs have decided to make changes to some of their dishes, taking on board criticisms made during the week by the veteran judge.

programme.title: South West Starter
programme.desc: Chef Josh Eggleton is back for a third time. Last year he made the national finals when his starter was shortlisted for the banquet, this year he intends to go one step further and cook at the banquet. One of his rivals last time, Jude Kereama is also back and out to do better than he did previously. The third competitor is newcomer Chris Wheeler who is originally from Swanage in Dorset.

programme.title: South West Fish
programme.desc: There are some exciting dishes on the menu as the three chefs from the South West tackle the fish course. Chef Josh Eggleton is hoping to impress with an original take on Bolognese, just one of six elements on his complex fish dish.

programme.title: South West Main
programme.desc: It is the main course and chef Chris Wheeler is out to show just how theatrical he can be, and his ideas are surprising everyone in the kitchen. No one knows quite what to expect, and the veteran chef is hoping it tastes as good as it looks.

programme.title: South West Dessert
programme.desc: It is the dessert course, and it is Josh Eggleton who has come up with the most ambitious dessert. He is creating his own self-serve ice cream made from vegetables, and making everything from scratch including toppings and syrups.

programme.title: South West Judging
programme.desc: It is the head to head and the South West region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. They are joined by guest judge, journalist and restaurant critic, Grace Dent.

programme.title: North West Starter
programme.desc: Two newcomers to the competition are challenging reigning North West champion Matt Worswick. Adam Reid is head chef at Manchester's Midland hotel and Kim Woodward, who made history when she was appointed Head Chef at the Savoy Grill.

programme.title: North West Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and reigning North West champion Matt Worswick has reason to be confident. However, Kim's confident she has got one up on Matt by baking her own black bread unlike Matt who's taking a shortcut.

programme.title: North West Main
programme.desc: It is the main course of the North West regional heat and the scores mean this is a crucial round. Matt Worswick may be the reigning champion, but he is not yet assured of a place cooking for the judges, and he is feeling the strain.

programme.title: North West Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the three North West competitors are getting creative, producing some of the most original and stunning desserts. All three chefs are working in a hot kitchen, the tension is palpable, and this time one chef will go home.

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton, and guest judge Lady Claire MacDonald OBE. There are standout dishes from both chefs making it a difficult contest to judge.

programme.title: Wales Starter
programme.desc: Three of the finest chefs from Wales are competing to be crowned champion. Two chefs are back for a second time: Phil Carmichael, from Cowbridge, South Wales, is executive chef at Berners Tavern in London, and Adam Bannister is chef and co-owner of Slice in his home city of Swansea. Adam was crowned Welsh champion last year so this year Phil is back with something to prove. He plans to go home raising the flag for Wales. The third chef is newcomer Andrew Birch, also from Swansea.

programme.title: Wales Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and newcomer Andrew Birch is confident - he is passionate about seafood. He is celebrating the cockle, which is harvested near his home city of Swansea. Adam Bannister has created an alter ego, Captain Bannister, for his modern take on the old boil-in-the-bag fish dinner, and Phil has chosen to revamp the classic prawn cocktail.

programme.title: Wales Main
programme.desc: Phil Carmichael is serving up his version of an OBE, a refined take on onions, bacon and egg. Adam is planning to serve up wild boar on a spit, while Andrew turns up the heat when he combines strong Japanese flavours with a traditional roast.

programme.title: Wales Dessert
programme.desc: It is the dessert course and one chef will go home. Phil Carmichael is determined it won't be him but not everything is going to plan when he tackles his "Cup of Tea for Ma'am". One of the accompaniments to his Earl Grey panna cotta just won't work. He has to make a difficult decision.

programme.title: Wales Judging
programme.desc: It is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from Wales are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, blogger and food writer Rosie Birkett.

programme.title: Central Starter
programme.desc: Three newcomers are competing to become regional champion. Daniel Smith, a former head chef for the Roux brothers, now runs his own restaurant in his beloved home county of Norfolk. Andrew Scott's worked with the best in the business, and he's concentrating on telling powerful stories as well as delivering perfect flavours. Danny Gill is a former head chef at Daniel Clifford's two-star restaurant Midsummer House.

programme.title: Central Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are using some of the UK's best seafood: lobster, salmon and Cornish crab. Danny Gill is a chef who likes to use the very latest equipment to create the most intense flavours. He's going to great lengths to maximise the taste of his cucumber consommé, and it is causing a lot of interest in the kitchen.

programme.title: Central Main
programme.desc: Two chefs are cooking venison. Danny Gill is making a venison wellington, inspired by his Dad, a former RAF chef who has served up wellington for royalty at many air force banquets, while Andrew Scott has sourced his venison from the Queen's Scottish estate, Balmoral.

programme.title: Central Dessert
programme.desc: This week three chefs from the central region are fighting to be crowned champion. One competitor will go home, only the two highest scoring chefs will make it through to the judging chamber. Danny Gill is facing his toughest day yet, choosing to make a staggering eight elements for his imaginative dessert.

programme.title: Central Judging
programme.desc: The Central region's two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort, for the very first time. Joining them in the chamber is guest judge Enam Ali MBE, a food entrepreneur who set up The British Curry Awards.

programme.title: London & South East Starter
programme.desc: Three of the most exciting talents from London and the South East region are competing for a place in the national finals. Head chef Mark Froydenlund runs Marcus Wareing's two-star restaurant. Russell Bateman is head chef at The Grove in Hertfordshire and Ronnie Murray who heads up the Hix Restaurant group.

programme.title: London & South East Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and chef Russell Bateman is celebrating the diversity of his beloved home town of London - by combining lobster with jerk spices for an ambitious fish course with seven key elements. Ronnie Murray's taking a risk with an ingredient which is close to the veteran judge's heart and is planning to serve it at three different temperatures, warm, deep-fried and frozen. And two Michelin-starred Mark Froydenlund is planning a novel way to present his dish.

programme.title: London & South East Main
programme.desc: It's the all-important main course and returning contender Mark Froydenlund is banking on it being his strongest dish. Russell Bateman is creating a beef dish, and Ronnie Murray's mixing a crown of lamb with a curried filling.

programme.title: London & South East Dessert
programme.desc: It's the dessert course and the final chance for three of London and South East's most competitive and talented chefs to get through to the judging chamber, today the veteran judge will send one chef home.

programme.title: London & South East Judging
programme.desc: It is the head to head and the two highest scoring chefs from the London and South East region are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. Joining this week as guest judge is Kevin Gould, an award-winning food writer.

programme.title: North East Starter
programme.desc: Mini Patel is back for a second attempt at the north-east regional title, but he is competing against two young newcomers, Tommy Banks and Chris Archer. In 2015 Mini went home after the dessert course, so he is hoping to keep better control of his nerves this year.

programme.title: North East Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and two chefs, Tommy and Mini, have very similar ingredients - both are cooking mackerel. However, Mini is trying an original beetroot sorbet while Tommy is using wild woodruff and oyster leaf from his own garden. Chris Archer has chosen the king of the sea, turbot, but there is controversy in the kitchen.

programme.title: North East Main
programme.desc: It is the main course of the north-east region and overnight there has been a dramatic development. It is a tough and emotional day for the chefs as they react to the news, but they battle on in a bid to present a perfect dish with venison and Wagyu-Angus beef - the meat of the day.

programme.title: North East Dessert
programme.desc: It is a highly emotional day for one of the chefs as he prepares a dish which is inspired by and a tribute to his own great Briton, his late grandfather. However, all does not go to plan, and the chef ends up making one key element three times in a bid to achieve perfection.

programme.title: North East Judging
programme.desc: The two chefs are cooking for judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton for the very first time. Joining them as guest judge is John Williams MBE, the executive head chef at The Ritz, the only hotel to hold a royal warrant for banqueting.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Starter
programme.desc: It is Chris McGowan's third time; however, he is facing tough competition from Mark Abbott, head chef at Daniel Clifford's two Michelin-star restaurant, Midsummer House, and also from Eddie Attwell who has just completed a year as head chef at Ardtara Country House in Upperlands.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Fish
programme.desc: Mark Abbott is pushing himself again plating up a complex fish course of the very finest produce. He is calling it Shellsational but at the last minute he forgets a key element. Returning chef Chris McGowan is refining cod and chips and Eddie Attwell is getting classical with the king of the sea, turbot. The repartee is relentless as the chefs jostle for top place on the leader board. Once again there is plenty of emotion as the veteran chef delivers the scores.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Main
programme.desc: It is the main course and returning Chef Chris McGowan is feeling confident, but part of his dish involves making his own venison sausages to serve with a venison rack, and getting it all done in time is straining his emotions. Eddie Attwell is also serving the meat but with a traditional Northern Irish dish called Dock pudding. Mark Abbott is pushing himself again; he is using wagyu beef and serving it with tongue and corn cooked in a variety of ways.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Dessert
programme.desc: The three chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking their desserts and one chef is on course for a historic score, he could beat his boss - a veteran of GBM - and achieve more marks than anyone has done throughout the history of the competition.

programme.title: Northern Ireland Judging
programme.desc: It is the head-to-head. The two highest scoring chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, restaurant critic and Editor-at-Large of the Independent, Amol Rajan.

programme.title: Finals Starter
programme.desc: It is the national finals of 'Great British Menu'. Before cooking starts the eight champions are called to London's Southbank to get a sight of the prize, the chance to cook at a banquet held at the Palace of Westminster, in celebration of everyday Great Britons honoured by the Queen. It has a huge impact on every one of the chefs, each is determined to do all he can to get a dish to the banquet.

programme.title: Finals Fish
programme.desc: It's day two of the national finals, and the eight champions cook their fish courses. This year's challenge has been to produce dishes that are a lasting legacy to the New Elizabethan Age. They must showcase the transformation in British cuisine during the Queen's historic 64-year reign.

programme.title: Finals Main
programme.desc: It's main course day, the one course every chef wants to cook at the banquet. The chefs' dishes will be judged by Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton along with guest judge John Williams MBE, executive chef of The Ritz.

programme.title: Finals Dessert
programme.desc: It's the final day of the competition, and the last chance for the eight champions to get one of their dishes to the banquet for Queen Elizabeth II's Great Britons. Judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton will judge the dessert course and then decide on the banquet menu to be served at the Houses of Parliament. Joining them in the judging chamber is Grace Dent, restaurant critic, journalist and author.

programme.title: Banquet
programme.desc: The winning chefs arrive at the Palace of Westminster to cook for the Banquet of Great Britons. The chefs have been selected because their dishes showcase contemporary British cuisine and demonstrate the transformation in British food during the Queen's historic reign.

programme.title: London and South East Starter
programme.desc: The three chefs meet their surprise veteran judge and cook their starters. A dish celebrating childhood summer memories takes on a complicated courgette dish and a technically tricky take on the cucumber sandwich.

programme.title: London and South East Fish
programme.desc: The atmosphere in the kitchen gets even more intense as all the chefs take risks with their dishes. Mike Reid, executive chef at M Restaurants in London, shocks when he pairs his fish with some highly unusual flavours.

programme.title: London and South East Main
programme.desc: The kitchen is filled with smoke as the three chefs prepare their summer-themed mains. Selin Kiazim is in her element, preparing a feast inspired by the summer barbecues. Mike Reid uses wagyu beef. Tom Kemble uses juniper branches to smoke his meat.

programme.title: London and South East Dessert
programme.desc: All three chefs are feeling the pressure as they attempt their technical summer desserts. With only the two highest scorers going through to the regional final, who will be sent home?

programme.title: London and South East Judging

programme.title: South West Main

programme.desc: All three chefs are honouring Wimbledon and the British summer with their technically challenging strawberry desserts. Only the two highest scorers will go through to cook for the judges.

programme.title: South West Judging

programme.desc: Tom Parker is eager to impress with a salad that includes 10 elements. Meanwhile, Paul Askew, hopes his traditional techniques will triumph over his younger competitors, and Ellis Barrie is taking a risk with a creative cucumber and oyster starter.

programme.title: North West Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the atmosphere in the kitchen gets even tenser as the three newcomers begin to understand the perfection and skill the veteran chef demands. Ellis Barrie attempts to create the flavour of a summer barbecue.

programme.title: North West Main

programme.title: North West Dessert

programme.title: North West Judging
programme.desc: The two remaining north-west chefs must cook their entire taste of summer menus again. The guest judge is Greg Rusedski, former British number one, who understands the high standards expected at Wimbledon.

programme.title: North East Dessert
programme.desc: Dessert is the last chance for the chefs to secure a place cooking for the judges and the pressure in the kitchen is intense. All the chefs are using unusual ingredients in their desserts.

programme.title: Theater Stained Glass Window, Propeller Clock and Shoe Stretcher
programme.desc: Stained-glass expert Matthew Nickels tries to recreate a window; horologist Steve Fletcher works on restoring a clock fashioned from the propeller of a World War I plane downed in France; a shoe stretcher loosens up.

programme.title: Georgian Desk, Boulle Clock and Elephant on Wheels
programme.desc: Clockmaker Steve gets busy restoring an intricate Boulle-work clock that hasn't ticked for 15 years, while soft toy repairers Julie and Amanda attempt to bring a threadbare elephant back to life.

programme.title: Treasure Chest, Life Guard Helmet and Rabbit Toy
programme.desc: Matthew Boultwood attempts to restore a piece of British military history; a ceremonial helmet hailing from the Life Guards' regiment.

programme.title: Peter Pan Gramophone, Child's Rocking Chair and Cash Register
programme.desc: Gramophone expert Tim Weeks works on restoring a portable Peter Pan gramophone; Sonnaz and Will work in a child's rocking chair; Steve tries to fix a broken vintage cash register that has been in a family business for generations.

programme.title: Big Ted and Little Ted, Victorian Lamp Post and Steam Car
programme.desc: Dominic Chinea has to future-proof an old Cornish museum sign; Steven Fletcher has to steer an old clunker back onto the road; Julie and Amanda start treatment on George, a very special teddy who has lost one of his eyes and his growl.

programme.title: Caputo Painting, Tricycle and Barometer Clock
programme.desc: Steven Fletcher and William Kirk combine their expert knowledge of clocks and woodwork to repair a broken barometer.

programme.title: Pub Sign, Spaceship Toy and Majolica Vase
programme.desc: Ceramics expert Kirsten Ramsay gets to work on a stunning Majolica Vase, which has fallen victim to more than one accident over the years, including a broken lid.

programme.title: Art Nouveau Mirror, Phonograph and Writing Case
programme.desc: A customer has a knotty nautical problem that leaves furniture restorer Will Kirk all at sea. Jay Blades and Tim Weeks get a vintage gramophone looking and sounding like new. Soft toy specialists Amanda and Julie take on a young lady suffering the effects of years of love and affection.

programme.title: War Watch, Louis Vuitton Trunk, Butter Churn
programme.desc: Clockmaker Steve Fletcher tackles a pocket watch that's come all the way from Holland; metalworker Dominic Chinea and master cooper Alastair Simms fix an ancient butter churn; leather expert Suzie Fletcher restores a trunk made by Louis Vuitton.

programme.title: Smyth Painting, Monkey Stick, Seaside Telescope
programme.desc: Jay Blades and the team bring three treasured family heirlooms back to life; guitar restorer David Kennett tackles a worn out bass guitar belonging to Tony Wilson, founding member of 1970s funk band Hot Chocolate.

programme.title: Chalet Music Box, Globe, Garnet Bracelet
programme.desc: Music box expert, Stephen Kember, and furniture restorer Will Kirk come together to work on a music box that is housed in a replica Swiss chalet.

programme.title: Riding Crop, Grandad Chair, Hungarian Vase
programme.desc: Sonnaz Nooranvary takes on a battered but beloved armchair; Steve and Suzie Fletcher try their hand at restoring a WWI-era military riding crop; Kirsten Ramsay tackles a damaged Hungarian vase.

programme.title: Yukio Tani, Porcelain Clock, Nursery Chair
programme.desc: Art conservator Lucia Scalisi works on a 1930s portrait of a Japanese martial arts master; upholsterer Sonnaz Nooranvary restores a Victorian chair; horologist Steve Fletcher and ceramics expert Kirsten Ramsay restore an ornate porcelain clock.

programme.title: Painted Glass Window, Art Deco Lamp, Sea Chest
programme.desc: Resident horologist Steve Fletcher and ceramics restorer Kirsten Ramsay work to fix an art deco lamp; stained-glass expert Matthew Nickels completely overhauls a precious painted window.

programme.title: Fred Bear, Piano Stool, Statuettes
programme.desc: Soft toy restorers Amanda Middleditch and Julie Tatchell work their magic on an old teddy called Fred; silver smith Brenton West comes to the rescue of a pair of Art Deco statuettes that miraculously survived the Blitz.

programme.title: Wall Clock, Piano Make-up Compact and Cradle
programme.desc: Resident clock expert Steve Fletcher restores an 18th century wall clock; Caner Rachael South restores a beautiful wicker cradle that has been in use for generations; Brenton West fixes a much loved powder compact, made in the shape of a piano.

programme.title: Dogs of Fo, Racing Car and JW Painting
programme.desc: Art conservator Lucia Scalisi repairs a much loved landscape; clockwork expert Steve Fletcher gets a treasured clockwork toy car back on the road; ceramics expert Kirsten Ramsay tackles a damaged porcelain Chinese guard dog.

programme.title: Barmaid Clock, Silver Mirror and Eames Chair
programme.desc: Resident clock expert Steven Fletcher receives an unusual time piece; Silversmith Brenton West is tasked with restoring a precious hand mirror that has lost its glass; specialist furniture restorer, Graeme Mancha, overhauls an Eames chair.

programme.title: Meissen Clock, Typewriter and Bomber Jacket
programme.desc: Resident clock expert Steven Fletcher and ceramics conservator Kirsten Ramsay toil on a fragile 19th Century clock; Saddle maker Suzie Fletcher answers a mayday call to restore a WW2 pilot's bomber jacket.

programme.title: Rocking Horse, Nursery Plaque and Stereoscope
programme.desc: Furniture restorer William Kirk takes on a cherished family rocking horse; ceramics conservator Kirsten Ramsay works wonders on a Royal Doulton plaque.

programme.title: Leaf Chair, Hercules and Smokers' Stand
programme.desc: Suzie Fletcher and Sonnaz Nooranvary restore a badly damaged leaf chair from the 60s; Matthew Boultwood rescues a 30 kilo cast iron statue of Hercules; Will Kirk takes on an interesting smokers' stand with the help of restorer Steven Fletcher.

programme.title: Grandmother Clock, Magnifying Glass and Blighty
programme.desc: Kirsten Ramsay takes on a very rare Royal Doulton figurine of a First World War soldier; Steven Fletcher and Will Kirk combine their skills to piece back together a small long case clock; Brenton West tackles a treasured magnifying glass.

programme.title: Dutch Cane Chairs, Hornsey Vase and Military Chest
programme.desc: The team repairs an old military chest, needing new brass hinges and chains, a white Hornsea studio pottery vase from the 1950s which had a big piece broken off of it, and an antique cane chair which needs a full re-upholstering.

programme.title: Skeleton Clock, Giant Teddy Bear and Transistor Radio
programme.desc: The team tackles an antique skeleton clock, a gigantic teddy bear and beloved transistor radio of enormous sentimental value to its owner; they also look at a pair of German wire-cutters rescued from a WWI battlefield.

programme.title: Bass Guitar, End-Of-The-Pier Machine, Hand-Carved Belt
programme.desc: Jay Blades and the team bring three treasured family heirlooms back to life; guitar restorer David Kennett tackles a worn out bass guitar belonging to Tony Wilson, founding member of 1970s funk band Hot Chocolate.

programme.title: Weather Vane, Leather Rhino, Mini Jaguar
programme.desc: The team takes on a pocket sized racing car, a century-old and very rusty weather vane, and a much-loved but horribly damaged leather rhinoceros.

programme.title: Bike and Victorian Firefighter's Helmet
programme.desc: Jay Blades and the team restore a bike with a patriotic past, a threadbare teddy on wheels and a Victorian firefighter's helmet.

programme.title: Go-Kart, Handwork Leatherwork, Cat Figurine
programme.desc: The team takes on a dilapidated old go-kart, a handmade leather gun slip and a charming cat figurine that sparked a collectibles movement.

programme.title: Magician's Music Box, Penny Arcade, Push Along Horse
programme.desc: Jay and the team restore a music box with a magical connection, make over a much-loved push-along horse and revive a water-damaged penny arcade game.

programme.title: Theatre Chair, Bronze Locket, Inclined Plane Clock
programme.desc: Upholsterer Sonnaz Nooranvary revamps a family treasure with an intriguing history; a threadbare theatre chair once played host to thousands of theatre-goers in the famous Derby Hippodrome.

programme.title: Rocking Horse, Pinball Machine, Barograph
programme.desc: The team tackles a 1930s pinball machine, an antique weather device and a rocking horse that holds huge sentimental significance for its owner.

programme.title: Penny Farthing, Leather Briefcase, Clocking on Clock
programme.desc: Vintage bike restorer Tim Gunn faces a huge challenge when 80-year-old Peter Swash arrives with an ancient penny-farthing in tow; master saddlemaker Suzie Fletcher takes on the repair of a battered leather briefcase with a very proud history.

programme.title: Cine Projector, Spinning Wheel, Wicker Chair
programme.desc: The team tackles a 1960s cine-projector, a charming wicker chair and a hand-crafted spinning wheel that has traveled all the way from Shetland.

programme.title: Barber's Pole, Enwonwu Painting, Writing Slope
programme.desc: Metalworker Dom Chinea takes on the challenge of a battered old barber's pole that stood outside a London barber shop for decades; fine art conservator Lucia Scalisi restores a significant early work by eminent Nigerian artist Ben Enwonwu.

programme.title: Miner's Lamp, Rug Covered Armchair, Antique Music Machine
programme.desc: The team tackles a miner's lamp that saved its owner's life.

programme.title: Harmonium, Sweet Dish, Doll's House
programme.desc: Jay and the team tackle a shattered ceramic dish, a handmade doll's house and a vintage harmonium that provided the soundtrack to many an East End knees-up.

programme.title: Radio from Dunkirk, Leather Gaming Case, Grandfather Clock
programme.desc: The team tackles a radio that survived the evacuation from Dunkirk, a battered leather gaming case and a grandfather clock with a poignant history.

programme.title: Concertina, Vintage Jigsaw, Cocktail Table
programme.desc: Accordion restorer Roger Thomas has a serious job on his hands to get a beautiful vintage concertina, dating from the late 19th century, working again.

programme.title: Tram Seat, Racing Game, Stained Glass Panels
programme.desc: Repairing an old tram seat; repairing a vintage 1920s racing game; repairing two stained-glass panels that hold precious memories for their owner.

programme.title: Pedal Car, Card Table, Salome Statue
programme.desc: Restoration of a toy pedal car; resurrecting a wobbly old baize-covered card table dating from the 1940s; rescuing a precious bronze statue by renowned French artist Claire Colinet, depicting Salome.

programme.title: Memorial Board, Cod Liver Ted, Beromat
programme.desc: Repairing a faded and misshapen wooden memorial board, which records the names of all the men of the village who served in WWI; a teddy bear needs attention; an iconic German-built Beromat one-armed bandit.

programme.title: Carousel Horse, Cat Teapot, Boat Puzzle
programme.desc: Dominic Chinea takes on the restoration of a once brightly colored wooden carousel horse; ceramics conservator Kirsten Ramsay is charged with the task of repairing a little cat teapot with an extraordinary wartime story behind it.

programme.title: Binoculars, Vintage Mechanical Money Box, Boxing Belts
programme.desc: Jay and the team tackle a set of binoculars salvaged from a WWII U-Boat, a vintage mechanical money box and two boxing belts with a proud and emotional history.

programme.title: Ventriloquist's Dummy, Running Trophy, Typewriter
programme.desc: The team tackle a ventriloquist's dummy, a 1920s typewriter and a precious athletics trophy that's the last remaining memento of a much-loved father.

programme.title: Whiskey Barrel, Swagger Stick, Baby Scales
programme.desc: The team restores a miniature whisky barrel, an antique set of scales and a military swagger stick with precious memories for its 93-year-old owner.

programme.title: Leather Pouffe, Model Spitfire, Silver Purse
programme.desc: The team restores a hand-carved Spitfire, and a much-loved leather pouffe.

programme.title: Family Portrait, Vintage Fountain Pen, Tiger Automaton
programme.desc: Today in the Repair Shop, the team restore a much-treasured family portrait, a precious vintage fountain pen, and a 130-year-old tiger automaton that has lost its growl.

programme.title: Carrom Board, Magic Duck, Scott Albums
programme.desc: A pair of albums charting Scott's expedition to the South Pole, a traditional Asian board game and a much-loved magic trick are restored by the team of experts.

programme.title: Photo Plate, Clockwork Tractor, WW1 Compass
programme.desc: Craftsman David Burville takes on the repair of a little clockwork tractor; Barry Phillips fixes an old military compass that has seen service in both world wars.

programme.title: Newsagent's Clock, Barber's Chair, Antimony Box
programme.desc: Jay and the team take on the repair of an old barber's chair and clock.

programme.title: Bagpipes, Welsh Crown, Tortoise Bell
programme.desc: The team restore a broken and battered set of bagpipes, used by a piper who served in the Royal Scots; a silver Eisteddfod crown; a quirky tortoise-shaped bell, that sat for years on the counter of a family-run butchers' shop.

programme.title: Quirky Train, Nautical 'Ditty Box', Doll
programme.desc: Clockwork maestro Steve Fletcher finds himself working on a remarkable train set designed and built by the celebrated cartoonist and inventor Rowland Emmet; furniture restorer Will Kirk takes on the challenging repair of a wooden nautical ditty box.

programme.title: Victorian Kaleidoscope, Carved Wooden Bench, Military Mementoes
programme.desc: The team restore a Victorian kaleidoscope, a carved wooden bench that plays a tune, and a pair of military mementoes belonging to an extraordinary soldier.

programme.title: Asko Table, Wind-Up Panda, Coconut Scraper
programme.desc: Will brings a mid-century coffee table back to life; Steve collaborates with Amanda and Julie on a wind-up toy panda dating from the 1960s; Dominic gets a rusted coconut scraper back into service.

programme.title: Portsmouth F.C Mascot, Cricket Ball, Ships Wheel
programme.desc: Suzie and Lucia save a piece of family history in a 1948 commemorative cricket ball; Dom and Will team up to restore a boat steering wheel; Kirsten, Amanda and Julie piece together a Portsmouth mascot that was first pinned at a FA Cup final in 1939.

programme.title: POW Satchel, Spy Catcher's Clock and Sea Serpent Pen Holder
programme.desc: Suzie restores a World War II soldier's blood-stained leather satchel; Steve repairs a Victorian clock; silversmith Brenton works his magic on a bronze sea serpent pen holder.

programme.title: Watering Can, Camel Saddle and Bobby Bear
programme.desc: Dom restores a former fairground family's watering can with help from Brenton; Suzie and Will tackle a miniature camel saddle from Malaysia; Amanda and Julie repair a 100-year-old RAF mascot bear to honor a brave airman and father.

programme.title: Toy Cannon, Inkwell, St. Fiacre Statue
programme.desc: Jay Blades and the team bring more treasured family heirlooms, and the memories they hold, back to life; ceramic conservator Kirsten Ramsay carefully restores a cherished but chipped piece of 1960s pottery.

programme.title: Shell Stool, Classic Speedo and Wicker Crib
programme.desc: The team take on a beautiful, carved walnut piano stool, a defunct speedometer from a 1920s vintage car, and a wicker baby crib that has been at the heart of a family for generations.

programme.title: Chiefy, Bird Brooch, Far East Travel Trunk
programme.desc: Richard puts the sparkle back in a tiny bird brooch cherished by four generations; Amanda and Julie take a handmade rag doll from shabby to shipshape; Will and Brenton revive a well-traveled trunk that's journeyed 6,000 miles.

programme.title: Sidecar, Papier Mache Table and Military Drum
programme.desc: Dom gets a bicycle sidecar back on the road again; Will pieces together a Victorian sewing table; Pete repairs a drum which has seen frontline action in both the first and second world wars.

programme.title: Reel to Reel, Strong Woman's Dress, Wind-Up Car
programme.desc: The team take on a broken tape recording machine, a beautiful green sequined stage costume that once belonged to a 1950s strong woman and a windup car that's gone kaput.

programme.title: Piggy Bank, Knackler Gramophone, Prussian Helmet
programme.desc: The team take on a home-made gramophone that has lost its voice, a piggy bank smashed and shattered into pieces, and a 19th century German ceremonial helmet.

programme.title: Seesaw, Bedspread, Shooting Stick
programme.desc: Metalworker Dominic Chinea is challenged to revive a rare and curious children's toy; hand embroidery expert Sara Dennis is given the challenge of reviving a century-old embroidered bedspread.

programme.title: Victorian Highchair, Smugglers Telescope, Tippling Stick
programme.desc: The team take on a tippling stick thought to have belonged to King George V, a nearly 200-year-old telescope that needs the eye of optics expert Richard Biggs, and a Victorian high chair that transforms into a rocking chair.

programme.title: Gold Nugget Ring, Bologna Box, Fire Bucket
programme.desc: The team tackle a small but very precious family heirloom: a 170-year-old gold ring, with intricate detailing, that is currently in pieces, a jewelry box bought in Italy, and a 200-year-old fire bucket, which is on the brink of collapse.

programme.title: Garden Bench, Triumphator Calculator, Bridle
programme.desc: Dom saves a beloved garden bench; Steve repairs a Triumphator calculator that hasn't performed a calculation in decades; an antique bridle needs some serious TLC from Suzie.

programme.title: Scooter, Powder Box, Bottle Stopper
programme.desc: Tim restores a rusty 1930s scooter; Brenton works on an engraved powder compact with a theatrical past; Will rejuvenates a whimsical vintage bottle stopper.

programme.title: Boxing Gloves, Cigarette Box, Laurel and Hardy Bike
programme.desc: The team take on a pair of tired and torn boxing gloves that once belonged to the owner Andy's uncle, a broken ostrich egg cigarette box and a 1950s toy bike gifted to the owner's brother by none other than Laurel and Hardy.

programme.title: Sausage Making Machine, Postcard Album and Samovar
programme.desc: Dom overhauls a vintage sausage making machine; Chris adds a sturdy new spine to a crumbling Edwardian album full of treasured family postcards; Brenton transforms a hot water urn that was a wedding gift over half a century ago.

programme.title: Doorstep Ted, Banjulele, Tea Caddy
programme.desc: Julie and Amanda repair a toy bear received as a gift in the 1940s; Pete restores a 1920s banjulele that is a hybrid of a banjo and a ukulele; Will revives a century-old tea caddy that has served as a precious box of memories.

programme.title: Adventurers Case, Homemade Telescope, Danzig Bowl
programme.desc: Suzie and Lucia revive a briefcase once owned by a father and an intrepid traveler; Richard and Dom get an ingenious, if unorthodox, telescope working again; Kirsten repairs a decorative bowl that survived the Nazis but was broken by a clumsy cat.

programme.title: Desk, Bear Scrapbook and Wind-Up Train
programme.desc: Christopher and Louise team up to rescue a 1950s scrapbook; Will restores a desk; Steve repairs the engine on a wind-up train; Lucia is on hand to give the bodywork a new life.

programme.title: Military Chess Set, Syrian Chair, Doll
programme.desc: Expert Brenton West takes on a pewter chess set representing the War of Independence; Will Kirk shows off his skills on an intricate X-shaped chair from Syria; toy restorers Amanda and Julie help a wartime mascot doll get fit for service again.

programme.title: Rugby Trophy, Sewing Machine, Accordion
programme.desc: Brenton restores a treasured rugby trophy from the early 1900s; Dom repairs a Victorian sewing machine; Roger brings back the voice of a 1930s accordion in a sorry state.

programme.title: Writing Bureau, Ploughing Trophies, Dancing Clogs
programme.desc: Will repairs a cherished family writing bureau; Brenton restores gold-plated trophies from the 1950s World Ploughing Championships; Suzie is intrigued by a pair of dancing clogs that were handmade over a century ago.

programme.title: Clock, Bear, 3D Photo Viewer
programme.desc: Steve restores an art deco chiming clock; Julie and Amanda tend to a beloved 65-year-old teddy bear; Brenton repairs a 3D photo viewer from the 1950s.

programme.title: Desilusión
programme.desc: Simón es el nuevo fotógrafo de la escuela, se enamora de Roberta. Por su parte, José se entera de que su tutor también vivía en la calle.

programme.title: Probando resistencias
programme.desc: Roberta se va con el fotógrafo y Diego se pone celoso. Tomás le dice a Roberta que Diego apostó con él, ella se pone muy triste. Además, Miguel planea descubrir a Gastón.

programme.title: Novios mayores
programme.desc: Gastón le miente a Franco y le dice que no está saliendo con Mía. Simón sigue a Roberta hasta su casa de campo. Giovanni le pide perdón a Vico. Pascual les informa a los alumnos que Giovanni fue aceptado nuevamente en el colegio.

programme.title: Mi verdadero yo
programme.desc: Giovanni presenta a sus padres frente a todos sus compañeros y les pide disculpas por negarlos. Por su parte, Roberta tiene un accidente en una motocicleta.

programme.title: Reencontrando el amor
programme.desc: Simón trata de convencer a Roberta para que regrese al colegio. Lupita le dice a Mía que terminando el año escolar Miguel se regresa a Monterrey. Franco acepta que Mía y Alma sean amigas.

programme.title: Aliados
programme.desc: Franco le pide ayuda a Miguel para separar a Mía y Gastón. Mía se molesta al enterarse de que Miguel trabajará con su padre.

programme.title: Ladrona de exámenes
programme.desc: Pilar trata de golpear a Lupita por decirle a su madre que ella robó los exámenes y Luján la defiende. Celina borra a Lupita de la lista de invitados al cumpleaños de Mía como venganza por decir que Pilar se robó los exámenes.

programme.title: Beso de amor
programme.desc: Gastón le asegura a Mía que se vengará de Miguel. Diego le confiesa a Roberta que sigue enamorado de ella y la besa.

programme.title: Carta misteriosa
programme.desc: Jacobo dice que RBD no podrá seguir tocando en el café, ellos se molestan, pero saben que no pueden hacer nada. Mía encuentra una extraña carta dirigida a Lupita.

programme.title: Acuerdos sorpresas
programme.desc: Mía y Roberta se enteran de que sus papás se encargarán de organizar su fiesta. Por su parte, Simón le dice a Roberta que hará publicidad para que la banda RBD de un concierto en un teatro.

programme.title: Complot
programme.desc: Miguel y Mía confrontan a Celina y ella confiesa que escribió la carta influenciada por Pilar y le pide perdón a Lupita.

programme.title: Maldades
programme.desc: Diego no quiere que su papá vea la propaganda de RBD. Mientras tanto, José recibe un regalo de su tutor. Roberta entierra el vestido que usaría Mía en su fiesta.

programme.title: Duelo de divas
programme.desc: Roberta está muy preocupada porque destruyó el vestido de Mía por las razones equivocadas. A pesar de su arrepentimiento, Mía se entera y casi la mata.

programme.title: La disculpa
programme.desc: Roberta le pide una disculpa a Mía por haberle tirado su vestido, pero Mía no piensa discutir más ahora que llegó el día de su fiesta. Por otro lado, Alma le regala a Roberta una moto.

programme.title: El día de la fiesta
programme.desc: Marcelino le dice a Roberta que su hermano lo obligaba a robar. Pilar le explica a Enrique que planeaba arruinar la fiesta de Mía y Roberta porque no la invitaron. Franco descubre que Alma encerró a Valeria. Peter abandona a Valeria en una calle.

programme.title: Volviendo a amar
programme.desc: Roberta acepta ser novia de Simón. Mía le agradece a Roberta que le haya regalado su vestido. Roberta le dice a Mía que se le nota que adora a Miguel. RBD canta en la fiesta.

programme.title: Expresando sentimientos
programme.desc: Mía finge estar ebria y besa a Miguel. Peter renuncia antes de que lo corra Franco por Valeria. Diego le confiesa a Tomás estar enamorado de Roberta. Gastón se enfurece porque Mía termina con él. Alma le dice a Valeria que fue muy cruel con Mía.

programme.title: Miedo a enamorarme
programme.desc: Gastón amenaza a Miguel con revelar su venganza en contra de Franco y Mía. Simón y Diego tienen un enfrentamiento por Roberta. Miguel le exige a Mía que le diga a Gastón que no son nada. Peter le dice a Mía que fue él quien le envió la carta.

programme.title: Cambiando de padres
programme.desc: Peter le dice a Mía que la carta que recibió fue escrita por su mamá hace varios años. Franco se enoja porque Mía decide irse a vivir con Alma. Roberta piensa vivir con Franco si Mía vive en su casa. Alma y Franco discuten por Peter.

programme.title: La verdad sobre Miguel
programme.desc: Roberta acusa a Pilar de mentirosa. Roberta y Alma discuten por Mía. León necesita el lugar donde tocará RBD para su campaña. Gastón le dice a Mía que Miguel quiere vengarse de su papá porque cree que es responsable de la muerte de su padre.

programme.title: Indecisión
programme.desc: Diego está dispuesto a enfrentar a su papá por Roberta y la banda. Gastón le informa a Mía que escuchó a Celina vomitando. Roberta decide quedarse con Simón y no perdonar a Diego. Franco le regala a Miguel una casa para su familia y un cheque.

programme.title: El problema de Celina
programme.desc: Mía habla con Celina para pedir ayuda profesional para el problema de bulimia de la segunda. Los alumnos hacen un motín para que Madariaga les explique el porqué se va a ir del colegio. Miguel confía en que Franco no crea lo que le diga Gastón.

programme.title: RBD al descubierto
programme.desc: Madariaga les miente a los alumnos para que no pierdan el año escolar. León le dice a Gandía que en el colegio existe una banda llamada RBD. Diego hará lo que sea para que Roberta descubra que Simón la engaña.

programme.title: La venganza de Gastón
programme.desc: Roberta cree que Diego inventó que Simón es casado y que delatará a RBD con Gandía. Madariaga prefiere que sus alumnos estén enojados que tristes por él.

programme.title: El verdadero responsable
programme.desc: Gandía les advierte a los alumnos que serán expulsados del colegio los integrantes RBD. Franco le dice a Mía que fue Carlo quien provocó que quedará en la ruina y muriera el papá de Miguel. Luego, Franco acepta que Gastón proteja a Mía de Miguel.

programme.title: El sufrimiento de Miguel
programme.desc: Franco le dice a Carlo que pagará por estafar al papá de Miguel y es detenido. Luego, Franco abofetea a Miguel y le recrimina que haya traicionado su confianza. Gastón le dice a Miguel que su papá no murió en un accidente sino que se suicidó.

programme.title: Lejos de la verdad
programme.desc: Pilar cree que su papá tiene una relación con Alicia. Nico les dice a todos que Miguel piensa regresar a Monterrey. Alma graba una conversación donde Valeria acepta que odia a Mía. Celina se molesta con Mía y Vico por llevarla con una psicóloga.

programme.title: Propuesta inesperada
programme.desc: Alma no puede comprobar que Valeria odia a Mía, y Franco se enfurece porque habla mal de ella. Franco le dice a Mía que se casará con Valeria. Gastón humilla y golpea a Miguel y Roberta lo defiende.

programme.title: Doble cara
programme.desc: Roberta le reclama a Gastón que, por su culpa, José se fue. Miguel y Diego evitan que Gastón golpee a Roberta. Monserrat le pide a Roberta que deje a Simón por el bien de su bebé. Pascual castiga a Roberta y la encierra.

programme.title: La boda
programme.desc: Elena le dice a Miguel que su papá sabía que sus negocios eran riesgosos y que, después de irse a la quiebra, sufría fuertes depresiones. Peter le pide a Mía que acompañe a su papá en su boda. Alma y Mía llegan a la boda de Franco.

programme.title: La humillación
programme.desc: Ante el Juez, Valeria le dice a Franco que no se casará con él porque solo quería humillarlo. Miguel decide quedarse. Nico le pregunta a Lupita si se casaría con él.

programme.title: Traidor
programme.desc: Nico y Lupita están decididos a casarse. José descubre que Gastón informó a León sobre el concierto de RBD. Renata besa a Enrique por celos. Mía accede a tenderle una trampa a Gastón. Pascual les exige que renuncien al grupo o serán expulsados.

programme.title: Prueba gráfica
programme.desc: Franco está de acuerdo en firmar la carta para desintegrar a RBD. León quiere obligar a Diego a ser Político. Gandía le enseña a Gastón una foto besando a Mía, y él le exige a Mía que le diga por qué lo traicionó diciendo que la obligó a besarlo.

programme.title: El amor es lo más importante
programme.desc: Miguel se pelea a golpes con Gastón por defender a Mía. Ella le pregunta a Miguel si es posible que vuelvan a estar juntos. Diego interroga a Roberta sobre su relación con Simón. Todos los alumnos celebran la boda simbólica de Lupita y Nico.

programme.title: El destino lo arregla todo
programme.desc: Diego quiere ser amigo de Roberta; Miguel le pide perdón a Mía; Mayra convencerá a Lupita y Nico para que no dejen el colegio; Mía le ofrece a Roberta viajar a Orlando con ella y luego a Sudamérica; Diego se preocupa al ver a sus padres discutir.

programme.title: Buen viaje
programme.desc: Mabel le recuerda a Diego que lo ama; Madariaga les dice a sus alumnos que los niños de Chiapas lo necesitan; el señor Mendiola le exige a Gandía que reincorpore a Gastón de prefecto; Mía descubre que Roberta cambió su boleto por un viaje en crucero.

programme.title: Media hermana
programme.desc: Los chicos se divierten en Cuernavaca. Mía y Miguel pasan sus vacaciones juntos y se enteran de que han ganado un viaje. Tras despedirse de Nico en el aeropuerto, Lupita visita a su padre para conocer a su media hermana.

programme.title: Impulsivamente
programme.desc: Lola rechaza a Lupita. Diego es picado por una araña gracias a Roberta que está decidida a arruinarle el día. Lupita se entera de que Dulce es también su media hermana. Mía y Miguel se van de viaje.

programme.title: Cenizas de amor
programme.desc: Mía hizo arreglos para tener habitaciones separadas de Miguel. Roberta le cuenta a Diego que terminó su relación con Simón. Giovanni se entera de que sus padres sufrieron un desfalco y quedaron en la ruina. Diego encuentra a León con otra mujer.

programme.title: Nuevos año, nuevos retos
programme.desc: Empieza el nuevo ciclo escolar y ahora los alumnos tendrán que adaptarse a las nuevas reglas. Algunos cambios son demasiado para ellos. Roberta, indignada, comienza una huelga.

programme.title: El soplón
programme.desc: Gandía le advierte a Alma que no va a tolerar más indisciplinas de Roberta; Lisette encuentra a Giovanni en su casa; Roberta le dice a Lupita que Pilar otra vez las traicionó; Mendiola le dice a Gandía que cursará su maestría por Internet.

programme.title: Boda trágica
programme.desc: La profesora Hilda les informa a los alumnos que Hilario murió el mismo día que se casaron. Vico encuentra a Giovanni en la recámara de Florencia, su mamá. Miguel intenta seducir a Mía, pero lo rechaza.

programme.title: Atrapados en la Isla del Amor
programme.desc: Miguel le da una sorpresa a Mía y la lleva a una playa encantada lejos de todos, para poder pasar tiempo a solas.

programme.title: El castigo
programme.desc: Mía y Miguel descubren que la lancha no está. Mía tiene miedo de que Miguel la deje como lo hizo su mamá. Lupita y Teo serán los asistentes del profesor de Matemáticas. Castigan a Lupita por culpa de Lola.

programme.title: Testimonios
programme.desc: Mía y Miguel se pierden en una playa virgen, y no hay nadie quien los pueda rescatar. El padre de Diego trata de convencerlo para que declare en contra de su madre en el divorcio.

programme.title: Concierto privado
programme.desc: Roger le pide a Roberta un concierto. Diego cree que Roberta aún lo quiere, pero Tomás lo desanima. Roberta piensa darle la oportunidad a Diego de demostrarle que ha madurado.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: Miguel intenta que Mía reaccione y busca la manera de salir de la isla; Don Cosme abofetea a Giovanni por renegar de ser pobre; Roberta besa a Roger y Diego le dice que Verónica ya es su novia; Miguel encuentra una lancha y al regresar Mía no está.

programme.title: Terrible trampa
programme.desc: Miguel le promete a Mía no dejarla sola nunca más; Franco cree que Alma y Guillermo tuvieron relaciones sexuales; Leonardo le demuestra su apoyo a Celina al verla deprimida por la trampa del video; Gandía castiga injustamente a los alumnos.

programme.title: Falso amigo
programme.desc: Leonardo golpea a Rocco por defender a Celina. Gandía piensa que el busto que le regalaron los alumnos contiene una bomba.

programme.title: ¿Dónde será el ensayo?
programme.desc: Mía tiene un altercado con Sol, por adueñarse de su cuarto; Pilar le hace creer a Vico que Giovanni la engaña; Franco cree que Mía tuvo relaciones; Leonardo intenta que Lola quiera a Lupita; la banda RBD se reúne para acordar en dónde ensayarán.

programme.title: Rebelde
programme.desc: Mía se enfurece al ver que Sol coquetea con Miguel. El Sr. Mendiola le avisa a Gandía que está despedido. Lola no acepta hablar con Lupita. Gandía le avisa a Pilar que la sacará del colegio porque ya no podrá pagarlo.

programme.title: Dilema
programme.desc: Pascual anuncia su despido de la institución, todos lloran y no saben si decir la verdad para defenderlo ante el comité para que lo perdonen.

programme.title: Reunión
programme.desc: Mía se enoja al ver llegar a Sol y a su amiga a los ensayos de RBD. El enojo la hizo decidir terminar con el grupo. Llega el nuevo director.

programme.title: Nuevo trabajo
programme.desc: El nuevo director quiere que se lo respete y que mejor que ponerse contra los alumnos e imponerse cortándole el cabello a Santos, lo que hace que todos lo odien aún más.

programme.title: Altruismo
programme.desc: Mía dona parte de su ropa a los niños pobres, pero el director Font aprovecha su generosidad para quedar bien. Mía descubre que Sol y Miguel provocaron que regalara su ropa nueva. León obliga a Diego a firmar una acusación en contra de su madre.

programme.title: Fotografías inapropiadas
programme.desc: Lola saluda muy efusiva a Lupita. Font sorprende a Sol insinuándosele al profesor Gonzalo; Alicia encuentra en el escritorio de Font fotografías de varias adolescentes; Sol golpea a Mía con un balón; Sol se enfurece al ver a Mía con Miguel.

programme.title: Mala persona
programme.desc: Roberta le dice a Mía y a Miguel que le preocupa el futuro de RBD. Hilda y Alicia sospechan que Font no es una persona honesta. Teo le comenta a José que la quiere, pero siente que lo asfixia. Tomás le dice a Roger que le enseñará algo de Roberta.

programme.title: Reconciliación planeada
programme.desc: Tomás pretende mostrarle a Roger una grabación, pero José le roba el casete; Mía y Miguel planean que Roberta y Diego se reconcilien; Roberta se entera de que Roger está enfermo; Roger finge un ataque al corazón cuando Roberta termina con él.

programme.title: Injusticia
programme.desc: Font acepta que Santos realice un documental del colegio; Sol logra que despidan a Mayra por recriminarle su acoso al profesor Gonzalo; los alumnos se quejan de las injusticias del director; Lola obliga a Sol a pedirle perdón a Lupita.

programme.title: El perdón
programme.desc: El director les anuncia a los estudiantes que el profesor Gonzalo ha sido despedido del colegio por traspasar los vínculos entre docente y estudiante.

programme.title: Celos incontrolables
programme.desc: Miguel siente celos al ver a Mía con Gastón. El director Font ve a Sol en bikini e intenta besarla. Alma le ofrece a Mayra ser su asistente. Mía planea ayudar a Alma en su show junto a RBD.

programme.title: Las apariencias engañan
programme.desc: El padre de Diego habla con él pidiéndole que no ayude a Alma, ya que ahora su carrera política está en lo alto, mientras que el director es despedido.

programme.title: Una cuestión de confianza
programme.desc: Leonardo quiere ser novio de Lupita, pero Lola piensa que es con ella con quien quiere andar; el señor Mendiola les informa a los alumnos que el nuevo director del colegio es Pascual; Miguel se enoja con Mía por salir con Gastón y mentirle.

programme.title: Plan malévolo
programme.desc: León ensucia el agua del colegio para poder comprarlo. Roger se hace el enfermo para que Roberta lo cuide.

programme.title: Amor incierto
programme.desc: Quieren cerrar el colegio porque los inspectores determinan que las instalaciones no están en condiciones óptimas. Lola se lanza a los brazos de Leo y lo besa delante de Lupita. RBD actúa como grupo coreográfico de Alma, ocultos tras una máscara.

programme.title: La víctima
programme.desc: Pascual se siente un hombre afortunado; Lola insulta a Leonardo al saber que no está interesado en ella; Mía acepta dejar de ser amiga de Gastón; León le dice a Diego que es socio de la Elite; Gastón, al ver a Mía, finge que Miguel lo golpea.

programme.title: No todo es lo que parece
programme.desc: Mía le promete a Miguel alejarse de Gastón. Lupita le pide a Teo que finja que son novios, pero José los sorprende. Roberta y Diego se postulan a la presidencia de la sociedad de alumnos. Miguel es atacado por un par de matones.

programme.title: Precampañas
programme.desc: Alicia le hace brujería a Pascual. Roberta y Diego preparan sus campañas para la presidencia. Lola descubre a José y Teo besándose y piensa que están engañando a Lupita. Mía tiene un mal presentimiento sobre una carta dejada por Miguel.

programme.title: Campaña desleal
programme.desc: La carta de Miguel deprime a Mía y Gastón aprovecha para acercarse a ella. Lola amenaza a Teo por engañar a Lupita. Roberta enfrenta a Diego por su campaña desleal. Después de ver a Leo besar a Lupita, Lola la abofetea y la llama mentirosa.

programme.title: Secuestrado
programme.desc: Diego pide a Iñaki que se infiltre en el equipo de campaña de Roberta. Los secuestradores se ponen en contacto con Mía para pedir un rescate por Miguel. Lupita se distancia de Leo e intenta arreglar las cosas con Lola, pero esta la desprecia.

programme.title: La petición de rescate
programme.desc: Roberta le pide a Lola que le dé otra oportunidad a Lupita. Diego le pide consejo a León para ganar las elecciones. Mía no consigue reunir la cantidad solicitada por los captores, pero Franco llega con el dinero y se disponen a rescatar a Miguel.

programme.title: Autor intelectual
programme.desc: Guillermo quiere romper con Fátima y le pide ayuda a Alma. Lola ofrece su apoyo a Diego a cambio de correr a Lupita de la escuela. Franco y Mía entregan el rescate. Gastón es el autor intelectual del secuestro de Miguel.

programme.title: Falsa empatía
programme.desc: Gastón finge enfrentarse a los captores de Miguel y le ayuda a escapar. Diego intenta quitarle la credibilidad a Roberta. Franco echa a Guillermo de su casa. Gastón paga a sus cómplices y planea usar el dinero del rescate contra Miguel.
